summary.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 6.5% QoQ to INR162 crore with 15% EBITDA margin; FY26 PAT was INR5.78 crore after a INR48.8 crore impairment.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR13.2 crore versus INR9.5 crore in Q3, about 38% QoQ growth, driven by higher revenue and better operating performance. Full-year FY26 profit was INR5.78 crore, after an exceptional charge of INR48.8 crore on impairment of the investment in step-down subsidiary MFT, which is in insolvency in Germany. Consolidated revenue grew 9% QoQ to INR205 crore with EBITDA of about INR30 crore (15%) and PAT margin of 4.9%. Management flagged raw material inflation (aluminium, steel, LPG, tools, oils) from the Iran war, with partial and time-lagged customer pass-through.

segments.name: Standalone PCL (foundry and machine shop)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR162 crore, up 6.5% QoQ, with 15% EBITDA margin and 8% PAT margin. Foundry utilisation about 80% and machine shop about 90%.

segments.name: EMOSS (Netherlands, e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR29.47 crore vs INR23.9 crore in Q3. Management sees little growth in FY27 or possibly FY28 given volatile European conditions; new applications are at early stage, with scale-up expected within about 1.5 years.

segments.name: MEMCO
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue of INR14 crore. Modernisation of legacy equipment and operational improvements are expected to lift profitability; no margin figure given.

segments.name: India e-mobility (e-HCV)
segments.commentary: Electric heavy commercial vehicle platform developed and first vehicle delivered to a customer in Q4. Certification and homologation targeted within FY27; commercial deployment from April 2027 if validation succeeds. An MOU indicates INR60-70 crore annualised revenue from one customer and one product.

guidance_outlook: Capex of INR100-120 crore over about 3 years on foundry, machine shop, advanced manufacturing and automation; incremental top line expected at 1.5x-2x capex annualised, peaking in 2.5-3 years.

Solapur facility is civil-complete; machines for first two projects arrive from mid-2026, production starts Q1 FY27. Plant has 10 lines, about 200,000 machined camshafts per month at full build, phased.
New capex is expected to commission from April-May 2027 (early FY28), with the big ramp-up from April 2027.
Existing-line debottlenecking to add about 10-20% capacity, with programmes starting in July and September 2026.
Management expects EBITDA margin to improve slightly from the new assembled-camshaft programmes and automation, but declined to quantify it.
Raw material inflation is expected to hit margins in the near term. Management hopes the impact is short-term once the war eases.

qa_highlights.question: When will Solapur facility complete and what capacity will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Civil construction complete, utilities ready; machines for first two projects arrive from mid-2026 with production from Q1 FY27. Full build is 10 lines, about 200,000 machined camshafts per month, phased.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for EMOSS in Europe after the Q3 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is very volatile with two wars and subsidy issues; business is stable at current rate, with little growth expected in FY27 or perhaps FY28. New applications are in early phases, with any scale-up within about 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental revenue and margin impact of the INR1,500 crore order book and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined year-wise projections. Capex of INR100-120 crore is expected to yield incremental top line of 1.5x-2x capex annualised, peaking in 2.5-3 years. New assembled-camshaft projects are higher margin and automation should lift EBITDA margin slightly, not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact of aluminium and other raw material price rises, and pass-through timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a near-term margin impact as steel, LPG, cutting tools, oils and aluminium rose over 2-3 months. Customers compensate but not fully, with a time lag from transit and payment on about 40-50% export sales; management hopes the shock is short-term.

qa_highlights.question: Market size and diversification (defence, aero) for the e-HCV opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: e-HCV first vehicle delivered; certification expected within 6-8 months and commercial sale after. An MOU with one customer implies INR60-70 crore annualised revenue from one product. Management targets the 10-30 ton MCV/HCV niche and sees defence and aero only via M&A, with acquisitions being sought in India.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and growth drivers before new capex comes on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Foundry about 80% and machine shop about 90%. Management sees room within existing capacity, with debottlenecking adding 10-20% through July and September 2026 programmes; 90% considered sufficient, and the big ramp starts April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new capex commission and what is the revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning in April-May 2027 (early FY28). Analyst's INR200-250 crore peak revenue figure was confirmed as the 'at peak' potential over 2.5-3 years.

capex_capacity: Capex of over INR100 crore (INR100-120 crore per Q&A) over about 3 years across foundry and machine shop capacity, advanced manufacturing technologies and automation; incremental top line expected at 1.5x-2x capex annualised, peaking in 2.5-3 years.

Solapur facility is civil-complete with plant and utilities ready; machines for first two projects arrive from mid-2026, production starts Q1 FY27. Plant has 10 lines, about 200,000 machined camshafts per month at full build, phased.

New capex to commission around April-May 2027 (early FY28); big ramp-up from April 2027. Management referenced INR200-250 crore revenue potential from new capex at peak (analyst's figure, confirmed as 'at peak').
Current utilisation: foundry about 80%, machine shop about 90% (management said over 80-85% across foundry and machine shop). Management sees 90% as sufficient near-term ceiling.
Existing-line debottlenecking adds about 10-20% capacity on certain customer platforms; some already in place, others starting July and September 2026.
Solar capacity raised to 29 MW after second phase commissioned in FY26, expected annual saving of about INR24 crore.
demand_pricing: Standalone revenue INR162 crore, up 6.5% QoQ; consolidated revenue INR205 crore, up 9% QoQ.

Management cites new business awards from Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai, M&M, Tata Motors, Renault-Nissan and other international customers, with cumulative lifetime revenue of about INR1,500 crore over and above existing order book; execution period framed as about 5-6 years (analyst's cumulative INR1,500 crore order book interpretation confirmed as cumulative).

Raw material inflation over last 2-3 months (aluminium, steel, LPG, cutting tools, oils) linked to the Iran war; customers compensate partially and with a time lag. Brijesh cited aluminium up more than 50%; management did not dispute the figure.
Export share about 40-50% of business, which adds transit and payment lag.
EMOSS (Netherlands) revenue INR29.47 crore in Q4 vs INR23.9 crore in Q3; management sees stable operations but little growth in FY27 and possibly FY28 given volatile European conditions.
MEMCO Q4 revenue INR14 crore; no margin disclosed.
Management expects EBITDA margin to improve slightly from assembled camshaft programmes (higher value add) and automation; declined to quantify.
risks_watch: Raw material inflation (aluminium, steel, LPG, tools, oils) from the Iran war may compress margins near term, with partial and lagged customer pass-through.
European e-mobility (EMOSS) demand volatile; management expects little growth in FY27 and possibly FY28.

e-HCV commercialisation depends on certification and homologation (targeted within FY27) and on regulatory and compliance frameworks for retrofit; the earlier Tata Ace attempt was not pursued due to compliance and RTO issues.
New capacity dependent on machine arrivals from mid-2026 and commissioning in April-May 2027; any slippage delays the INR100-120 crore capex payoff.
Management declined to give year-wise revenue or margin guidance on the INR1,500 crore order book and its execution profile.
Monitor Q1 FY27 Solapur production start, debottlenecking delivery from July and September 2026, and whether MFT insolvency has further impact.
key_quotes: The company reported a net profit of INR13.2 crores compared to INR9.5 crores in the previous quarter, reflecting a growth of approximately 38%.
Right now, we are not able to share with you exact year-wise projections, and we are also refraining from sharing future numbers or financials.

While some -- while customers do compensate us, they will not -- they don't fully compensate us, and there might be also a time gap between when we are incurring that expense and when it is compensated for.
There are no OEMs that are present in this application.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term order book, capex and India e-HCV opportunity, but cautious and non-committal on quantification of margins, year-wise revenue and EMOSS growth. Management was evasive on the market size for e-HCV and on defence diversification, saying it would look at M&A instead. Management repeatedly declined to quantify future numbers while expressing confidence in direction. The tone was measured on raw material costs, which it called a short-term issue.

growth.why: Management guides incremental top line of 1.5x-2x the INR100-120 crore capex (peaking in 2.5-3 years), backed by Solapur capacity starting Q1 FY27 and new capex commissioning Apr-May 2027, plus ~1,500 crore cumulative lifetime awards from OEMs; no explicit FY27 revenue growth % was given and EMOSS sees little growth.
